root_cause: The navigation controller incorrectly sets aria-activedescendant to the item's data-value (store name) instead of the element's ID, causing assistive technologies to announce the wrong active option.
repair_strategy: Change the assignment in the update function to use the list item's ID attribute, which matches the expected ID format (e.g., autoCompleteJS_result_0).
expected_accessibility_effect: aria-activedescendant will correctly reference the ID of the active option element, allowing screen readers to announce the highlighted suggestion as intended.
functional_risks: If any other code depends on dataset.value being reflected in aria-activedescendant, it may break.
Ensuring that list items have stable, unique IDs is required; duplicate or missing IDs would cause incorrect behavior.
verification_requirements: After typing 'ma' and pressing ArrowDown once, aria-activedescendant on #store should equal 'autoCompleteJS_result_0'.
After a second ArrowDown, aria-activedescendant should equal 'autoCompleteJS_result_1'.
Pressing Enter should set the form's store field to the selected suggestion's name (e.g., 'Marina Park').
